why: We already have Windows-grounded fresh defaults and fresh ranges, but the remaining concern is host/UI surface parity: the visible AE parameter boxes, twirled groups, nested sections, and label layout may not match between Windows AEX and the current Mac port.

This request is for the user-facing After Effects effect panel surface, not algorithm output. The primary artifacts are screenshots plus the same full property tree metadata used by the fresh default capture.
Separating UI-surface parity from algorithm parity prevents us from misclassifying a host panel mismatch as image-processing drift.

inputs.description: Use a simple opaque 1920x1080 source layer. Pixels are not the point; the effect-controls panel is.

instructions: For each case, create a fresh comp and a fresh source layer.
Add exactly one OLM effect to the selected layer.
Do not edit any OLM parameter after adding the effect.

Capture the full selected effect property tree exactly as AE scripting exposes it, including hidden/group/no-value entries, property_index, match_name, name, enabled/active state, and value where readable.
Also capture UI surface screenshots from the Effect Controls panel on Windows AE.
Save at least two screenshots per effect: (1) the cold-start top-level collapsed/default-visible state, and (2) the fully expanded state with every twirlable OLM group opened as far as AE allows.
If a plug-in has long grouped sections that do not fit in one viewport, capture a scrolled screenshot sequence that preserves the visible control order from top to bottom.
Do not crop away the effect title, built-in compositing controls, or group headers if they are visible in the panel.
Record a short note if AE prevents a group from being scripted open or if some controls are only visible after another popup/checkbox state changes.

cases.reason: Capture the top-level visible box layout for the simple OLM Blur surface.
Capture the grouped threshold, edge, replace, and per-color block layout as Windows AE visibly presents it.
Capture front/back/noise group visibility and label order in the Windows panel.
Capture render/interpolation/blur groups, threshold controls, and color-box presentation as seen in Windows AE.
Capture the complex grouped box layout including ramp sections and ray-direction controls as actually shown by Windows AE.
Capture outer/inner/ellipse/noise box grouping and visible nested label structure.
Capture the visible v1 panel and whether any extra group boxes such as Smooth Range appear in the Windows surface.
Capture key/gamma/version grouping and visible control box shape in Windows AE.
Capture the simple single-control panel plus built-in AE effect box layout.

manifest_requirements: Record all selected effect property names, match_names, property_index, property_type, property_value_type, enabled/active state, and values where readable.
Record hidden/group/no-value properties too; do not omit them just because AE scripting cannot read a scalar value.
Keep ADBE Force CPU GPU / GPU Rendering as reference-only metadata, not as the execution-path label.
Return Effect Controls panel screenshots for each effect in both cold-start and fully-expanded forms.
If multiple screenshots are needed to cover one panel vertically, preserve order with numbered filenames and include a small note describing the scroll sequence.
Treat this as UI-surface evidence first; before_effects_frame and effect-output PNGs are optional supporting artifacts, not the primary deliverable.
mac_follow_up: Use the screenshots and property tree together as the Windows source of truth for user-visible AE panel shape.
Compare against refs/reports/mac_plugin_param_schema_20260629.json and the current Mac AE panel before treating any panel mismatch as algorithm drift.
